integrity cross-check against an independent second mirror (sha256):
  - mountainside_1k.gltf: DIFFERS sha256 vs https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Mainframe-Games/mainframe-engine/main/Examples/Forest/Assets/Art/Props/mountainside/mountainside_1k.gltf
  - textures/mountainside_diff_1k.jpg: MATCH sha256 vs https://media.githubusercontent.com/media/Mainframe-Games/mainframe-engine/main/Examples/Forest/Assets/Art/Props/mountainside/textures/mountainside_diff_1k.jpg
    note: the second copy's .gltf is an edited variant (Mainframe-Games adds occlusionTexture and renames image 'rough'->'arm');
    accessor counts (80,238 verts / 460,416 indices) and .bin byteLength (4,409,280) are identical; the copy staged here is the unedited export.

intended use: SM_CliffRock_A (large cliff rock 10-20 m) - PRIMARY. Weathered grey-brown rock face with lichen/moss, 10.2 x 5.2 x 10.5 m -> scale x1.4 for 14 m.

tech notes (verified 2026-10-28):
  mountainside_1k.gltf: Blender 5.2 glTF import OK, missing images: 0; 153,472 tris; 1 mesh object(s); bbox (m, X/Y/Z-up) [10.209, 5.247, 10.522]; materials ['mountainside']; textures: mountainside_diff 1024x1024, mountainside_nor_gl 1024x1024, mountainside_rough 1024x1024
  Normal map is OpenGL (+Y) -> tick "Flip Green Channel" in UE. *_arm_1k.jpg packs R=AO, G=roughness, B=metallic (linear, sRGB off).
  Origin is not at base-centre/-Y-front per catalog convention: re-pivot in the dai pipeline.
  Over the ~15k-tri budget for a non-Nanite mesh. Tested recipe (Blender 5.2): import glTF -> bmesh remove_doubles(dist=1e-5)
  (Poly Haven exports are split at every UV seam; without welding, Decimate stalls at ~40% of the input) -> Decimate COLLAPSE
  ratio = target/tris. boulder_01 66,122 -> 15,000 tris was visually indistinguishable at prop distance. Or keep full res for Nanite.
